text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: P99_LATENCY_SERVING_US-WEST-2 — p99 > 1200ms for 5m, SLO burn 78% (service: runtime-inference)
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: P99_LATENCY_SERVING_US-WEST-2 — triggered. <https://pagerduty.com/incident/REDW-91324|view incident>
alex: acked the pager :hand:
alex: quick context — I just noticed a spike at 15:42 UTC across multiple nodes in us-west-2 GPU pool. Graph: <https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/serving/latency?view=us-west-2>
maria: seeing heavy tail on requests, p95->p99 gap huge. Trying to correlate with recent deploys. Anyone roll anything to serving in last 30m?
sanjay: I rolled a canary of quantized-v2 to 10% of requests ~20m ago, but rollout should be isolated to canary pool. Will validate.
chloe: running quick query on request headers to see sequence length distribution:

```
SELECT seq_len_bucket, count(*) FROM requests
WHERE region='us-west-2' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY seq_len_bucket ORDER BY seq_len_bucket DESC LIMIT 10;
```

chloe: result: big uptick in seq_len_bucket >= 16384 (long-context) — roughly 12% of recent requests, baseline <1% before
maria: ah that explains it — long sequences blow up decode kernel times. GPUs are falling back to slower kernel path and some nodes hit GPU memory pressure which queues work on CPU -> huge tail
alex: can we throttle or reject extreme seq lens at edge? Ops, can we apply a temporary limit? :pray:
ops-bot: running policy patch: `edge-config set max_sequence_length 8192 --scope us-west-2 --reason "p99 mitigation"` — queued
ops-bot: policy patch applied to edge routers in us-west-2, propagation ~30s
sanjay: I'm going to abort the quantized-v2 canary rollout to eliminate variable. `deploy rollback quantized-v2 --env serving-canary-usw2`
sanjay: rollback complete. Canary traffic back to v1 for canary pool.
chloe: rechecking seq_len after edge patch — long requests dropped from 12% to ~0.5% within 40s. p99 trending down.
alex: nice. still seeing a handful of nodes with high GPU mem and queued tasks — I'll set `inference-pool drain` on 3 affected hosts to force work redistribution: 

```
infra drain-node --pool inference-usw2-gpu --node node-32-7
infra drain-node --pool inference-usw2-gpu --node node-32-9
infra drain-node --pool inference-usw2-gpu --node node-48-2
```

alex: drain commands issued.
ops-bot: autoscaler kicked in +8 GPUs to pool (policy: rapid-burst). New capacity available.
maria: p99 has dropped from 1300ms -> 340ms in the last 3 minutes. p95 stable ~80ms. SLO burn reduced to 12% and falling. 
alex: good. next steps: keep edge short-seq limit for next 30m, monitor for any client-side retry/backoff storms, and postmortem if kernel fallback identified as root cause
sanjay: opened ticket INF-5423 to track kernel perf regression on quantized runtime and to dig into driver/kernel interaction. linking logs: <https://logs.internal/redwood/INF-5423>
chloe: notifying small set of affected customers (email template ready) — will send after 10m if stable :email:
alex: handoff to on-call followup: @maria you will own post-incident follow-up? I'll stay in loop for rollback details.
maria: taking ownership of follow-up and postmortem. I'll gather traces, sample requests, and coordinate with runtime/infra teams. cc: @sanjay for canary rollout checklist
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by alex. Escalation stopped.
incident-bot: incident status: mitigated — p99 returning to normal. Please continue to monitor for 30 minutes and file followup tasks.
alex: thanks team. good warm handoff — if anything regresses page again. :thumbsup:
